Description: A Digital Object Identifier (DOI) is a character string used to uniquely identify a resource. A DOI name is divided into two parts, a prefix and a suffix, separated by a slash.
The prefix part of the DOI, assigned by a registration agency.
The suffix part of the DOI, chosen by the client to uniquely identify the resource.
The event state of the DOI,it determines the DOI's publication status.
The URL of the landing page for the resource that the DOI resolves to. This is a mandatory field for making a DOI findable.
Information about the type of the resource. Usually a recommended free-text description paired with a general resource type from a controlled list.
The main researchers or authors involved in producing the resource, in priority order.
Type of name of the creator.
The personal or first name of the creator.
The surname or last name of the creator.
Uniquely identifies an individual or legal entity, according to various schemes.
Examples: For an author with an @id sub-property: 'nameIdentifier': 'https://orcid.org/0000-0001-5727-2427', 'nameIdentifierScheme': 'ORCID', 'schemeURI': 'https://orcid.org/'

Description: The organizational or institutional affiliation of the creator. In the case of an organizational creator, it will often be the name of the institution to which that organization belongs to.
The names or titles by which the resource is known. At least one main title is required.
Type of title other than the main one.
The name of the entity that holds, archives, publishes, or otherwise distributes the resource.
The year when the resource was or will be made publicly available. This must be a four-digit year.
Subjects, keywords, classification codes, or key phrases describing the resource.
The name of the subject scheme or classification code or authority if one is used.
The URI of the subject identifier scheme.
The URI of the subject term.
Used for the subject term in the subject scheme.
Examples: 310607 of subject term “Nanobiotechnology” in the ANZSRC Fields of Research.

Description: Institutions or Persons responsible for collecting, managing, or otherwise contributing to the resource. Each contributor has the same sub-properties as a creator, but additionally has a contributor type.
Different dates relevant to the resource, such as creation, publication, or update dates. Each date entry must have a type indicating its meaning.
The type of date.
The primary language of the resource, specified using an IETF BCP 47 language tag.
Any other identifiers for the resource, such as a local identifier or a URL to a code repository.
Identifiers of related resources, along with the nature of the relationship (e.g., 'IsPartOf', 'HasVersion', 'Cites').
Description of the relationship of the resource being registered (A) and the related resource (B).
Information about related resources that are not identified by a formal persistent identifier. This can include descriptive text about the related item.
Unstructured size information about the resource.
Technical format of the resource, preferably using IANA media types.
The version number of the resource. It is recommended to use semantic versioning where appropriate.
Information about rights held in and over the resource, such as a license. It is recommended to use an SPDX license identifier and URI.
All additional information that does not fit in any of the other categories. May be used for technical information or detailed information associated with a scientific instrument.
Spatial regions or named places where the data was collected or is about. Can be a point, a bounding box, or a polygon.
Information about financial support (funding) for the resource. This includes the funder name, award information, and funder identifier.
The URI of the DataCite metadata schema version used. For this model, the value is fixed to the DataCite Kernel v4 schema URL.
Information about the larger resource that contains this resource, such as a journal or a book series. This property helps create parent-child relationships.
